title: Clairambault 1161
contents: Political notices concerning England and Flanders: English arms and the Tower, religious policy, ships bound for Spain, Genoese lending, foreign courtiers, and a reported plan to force entry at Hampton Court.
status: 6/6 pages transcribed; 2/6 pages deciphered; 4 more in part
fields: 51 accepted forms: 38 letter signs, 11 nomenclature entries, 2 nulls, 39 provisional unidentified labels
3,149 elements, 3,046 identified; 5 further wordlike groups not classified
Plaintext in the margin or below
Matching historical plaintext in the margin of f163r, in the same volume; the other five cipher faces have no established matching plaintext.

excerpt: Ce Seigneur **a par deulx fois escript et mandé à ceste royne qu’elle laissast passer en silence et dissimulation beaucoup de choses quant au faict de la religion en ce royaume afin de regaigner sa noblesse et peuple, et que son filz et elle y puissent regner et commander en plus grand repos.**
translation: This lord **has twice written and sent word to this queen that she should let many matters concerning religion in this kingdom pass in silence and dissimulation, in order to win back her nobility and people, so that her son and she may reign and command there in greater peace.**
